newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IOC says focussing on infrastructure.
newsitem.headline: India's IOC says focussing on infrastructure.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) said on Monday it is focussing on infrastructural growth, a critical constraint which is seen plauging the country's economic growth.

IOC chairman, R.K. Narang told shareholders on Monday at the company's annual general meeting IOC had evolved a strategy for growth which involved upgrading facilities for technology development, efficency and expansion of infrastructure and customer facilites.
IOC is India's sole importer of crude oil and refined products.
Narang said a new company, Indian Oil Tanking had been formed in collaboration with Oil Tanking GMPH of Germany and IBP for infrastructure development (construction and operating of bulk terminals).
"Visualising the future growth and potential of Liquefied Petroleum Gas as fuel in power and other sectors, plans have been initiated for infrastructure development and fuel management in this area."
"Projects of about 100 billion rupees are in hand and investments of over 250 billion rupees have been identified," Narang said.
The chairman said a grassroots refinery at Panipat will be commissioned in financial year 1997 and another is being set up on the east coast in collaboration with Kuwait Petroleum Corporation.
"The country's longest product pipeline from Kandla to Bhatinda of 1,443 km has been taken in operation, raising the total length of Indian oil pipelines to 5,293 km," Narang said.
IOC cancelled its tender to import a diesel tender scheduled for delivery in November, earlier this month with traders citing port congestions for the cancellation.
They said the refining major had already cancelled the monthly kerosene import tender at least twice this year for the same reason.
"There is some time-lag and a bit of queing up also," Narang told Reuters after Monday's meeting but stressed that IOC will focus its attention on infrastructure projects in the coming years.
"I don't deny that there is scope for infrastructure development. The government has done something for this like the granting of tax holidays for infrastructure firms," Narang said.
Analysts see IOC as one of the biggest beneficiaries of a phased deregulation of India's oil sector in the next few years.
Currently, a multitude of price and distribution controls place the Indian oil industry in a tightly regulated position.
